## $x_1$-wall corner refresh inside tangential ghost slabs {#sec-ch03-cornerrefresh}

### Summary

The tangential exchange fills the $x_2$ and $x_3$ ghost slabs with the neighbour's interior, but within those slabs the
$x_1$ ghost rows (the corners next to an $x_1$ wall) hold whatever the neighbour's wall wrote last, or stale values on
a periodic edge. A stencil with cross-derivatives, such as viscosity next to the wall, then reads a wall corner that
does not belong to this column. Re-applying the $x_1$ boundary function on the slabs makes those corners the wall
ghosts of the updated slab.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** After the tangential exchange, re-apply each $x_1$ boundary function except outflow inside the
exchange-owned $x_2$/$x_3$ ghost slabs, so the corners next to an $x_1$ wall match the updated column (Derivation).

**Data.** In/out: the ghost corner cells of the conserved (`hydro_u`) and scalar (`scalar_s`) arrays, in their own units.

**Placement.** End of every per-stage block sync, after the tangential exchange.

**Activation.** No switch; always on in the block sync, not in `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones`; panel seams need `custom` on $x_2$/$x_3$.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact, if each boundary function gives the same ghosts when called again on an $n_g$-wide slab.

**Evidence.** Cartesian and cubed-sphere cases plus check `[C19]`; spherical-polar unasserted (Tests).
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm t}$ the array length along a tangential direction, ghosts
included (count); $n_{\mathrm{slab}} = \min(n_g, \lfloor n_{\mathrm t}/2\rfloor)$ the width of each end slab the
refresh rewrites (count).

A tangential face whose own function already wrote the corner is skipped; such a face is called physical. On the
`slab` and `cubed` layouts that is every face with an installed, non-periodic function. On the cubed sphere the panel
edges keep the function the card named, so the refresh asks which function that is. The built-in `custom` no-op
writes nothing, so the edge belongs to the panel exchange and its radial-wall corners are refreshed. Any other
function, including a caller's own under the name `custom`, owns its corner and is skipped. The refresh is always on,
and it reaches the panel seams when $x_2$ and $x_3$ name `custom`, as every cubed-sphere card in the code's
`examples/` and `tests/` does.[^cr-src]

[^cr-src]: [source: `chengcli/snapy#337`, "Fix radial wall refresh at cubed-sphere panel seams": the identity rule
    `is_custom_noop` and its four `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` cases. The cards: `grep -l "layout: cubed-sphere"` over
    `examples/` and `tests/` at the pin finds 16 files, and each names `custom` on all four tangential faces.]

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; it is a consistency rule. For each installed $x_1$ bfunc that is not outflow, and each
tangential direction with more than one cell, the bfunc is called on the first and last $n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ cells of
that direction, with $n_{\mathrm t}$ and $n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ as above (`int g = ng < n / 2 ? ng : n / 2` in
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}), unless that tangential face is physical in
the sense defined below, in which case its own bfunc already wrote the corner. A `reflecting` $x_1$ wall on a block
none of whose tangential faces is physical is instead called once over the whole array: it mirrors each $x_1$ row
from that row's own interior, so the one call writes the same corner values as the slab calls and rewrites the other
$x_1$ ghost rows with the bits they already hold. The rule relies on the contract stated with the `BC_FUNCTION` macro:
a face function called again on a tangential slab must not depend on the slab's size and must give the same ghosts
({{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}). Outflow is excluded because its background must match the whole block
and it needs primitives.

**The predicate `physical`.** The faces are numbered $0, \dots, 5$ in the order $x_1$ inner, $x_1$ outer, $x_2$
inner, $x_2$ outer, $x_3$ inner, $x_3$ outer, so a face number of 2 or more is an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face. The refresh's
local `physical(face)` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}) answers in this
order:

1. false if no function is installed on the face;
2. false if the layout type is `cubed-sphere`, the face number is 2 or more, and the installed function is the
   built-in `custom_inner` or `custom_outer` (`is_custom_noop`, {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_custom_noop >}});
3. false if the face's boundary name starts with `periodic`;
4. true otherwise.

Step 2 tests the function itself, not its name. `is_custom_noop` asks the stored function for its target as a plain
function pointer and compares that pointer with `custom_inner` and `custom_outer`, whose bodies are empty
(`custom_inner`, {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp BC_FUNCTION overload=1 >}}). An empty function, a registered function
such as `reflecting_inner`, and any callable a caller installs in the block's function table all fail that
comparison, even when the face's boundary name is still `custom`. Step 2 reads the layout's type string, not the
coordinate, so it never applies on `slab` or `cubed`.

**What `physical` resolves to on each layout**, because the rule reads the installed functions and the layouts do
not install the same ones. On `slab` and `cubed`, construction removes the $x_2$ and $x_3$ function of a face that
has a neighbouring block or whose axis is periodic ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}), so
`physical` is false exactly on the tangential faces the exchange owns and the slabs there are refreshed; this is
the Cartesian and the spherical-polar case. On the cubed sphere that removal does not run at all (the whole step
is guarded by `type() != "cubed-sphere"`), so every face keeps the function the card named. A card that names
`custom` on $x_2$ and $x_3$ installs the built-in no-ops there, step 2 makes all four tangential faces non-physical,
and the radial-wall corners inside every panel halo are refreshed. With a `reflecting` $x_1$ wall that is the single
whole-array call, because no tangential face is physical; with any other $x_1$ function it is the two end slabs of
each tangential direction. A cubed-sphere face named anything else, `reflecting` by default, or holding a caller's
own function, stays physical, and its radial-wall corners are left to that function, as on any physical face. The
radial direction is not split on the cubed sphere ($p_z$ is forced to 1,
{{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_initialize >}}), so every cubed-sphere block
owns both $x_1$ walls and the refresh has something to re-apply there. Step 2 never touches the $x_1$ faces.

The refreshed corner is whatever the $x_1$ function computes from the updated column, so the rule is exact: it adds
no arithmetic of its own. For a `reflecting` wall the corner rows are copies of the mirrored interior rows with the
normal momentum negated, a copy and a sign change, which are exact in floating point.

The check enumerates the rule (`[C19]`).[^cr-c19] Over 35 $(n_g, n_{\mathrm t})$ pairs the two end slabs of width
$n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ never meet, which is what the minimum is for; and over the 140 combinations of
$(n_g, n_{\mathrm t}, \text{tangential face physical}, \text{periodic})$ the number of writers of a corner cell is never more
than one, so the exclusion is exactly what keeps the result independent of the order the bfuncs run in. The
enumeration is over the value of `physical`, so it covers the cubed-sphere step as well: step 2 changes which faces
are physical, not what happens once that is known.

[^cr-c19]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C19]`; a Python enumeration of the slab rule of the corner refresh in `src/mesh/meshblock.cpp` at the pin,
    CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The refresh runs at the end of every per-stage sync, on `hydro_u` as conserved and on `scalar_s` as scalar, after
both exchanges and before the scalar primitive is rebuilt. It changes only $x_1$ ghost rows inside the tangential ghost
slabs; the one call of a `reflecting` wall also rewrites the other $x_1$ ghost rows, with the values they hold. The
seam it repairs is a block seam on `slab` and `cubed` and a panel seam on the cubed sphere; the cells it rewrites are
the same in both. On a cubed-sphere block with `reflecting` radial walls and the built-in `custom` on all four
tangential faces, one call per wall writes the radial ghost rows of all four panel halos at once. The $x_2$-$x_3$
diagonal corner columns get only their interior cells from the exchange (@sec-ch03-exchange); that call mirrors
them into their radial ghost rows too.

: Code map of the corner refresh. {#tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code):

1. `physical` is false for a face with no function, for an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face of a `cubed-sphere` block whose
   function `is_custom_noop` accepts, and for a name starting with `periodic`; it is true otherwise
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
2. `is_custom_noop` returns true only when the stored function's target is the pointer `custom_inner` or
   `custom_outer` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_custom_noop >}}).
3. `refresh` loops over the two $x_1$ faces, skips a missing or `is_outflow` function and an $x_1$ axis of one cell,
   and calls the function on each tangential slab whose face is not `physical`, or, for a `reflecting` wall when no
   tangential face is `physical` (`all_owned`), once on the whole array ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
4. It runs for `hydro_u` and `scalar_s` with their types ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} for `refresh`).

**How to use it.** No key: the refresh runs in every per-stage block sync for each installed $x_1$ function except
`outflow`. A user boundary function must honour the `BC_FUNCTION` contract (same ghosts on any slab size). On the
cubed sphere, name `custom` on $x_2$ and $x_3$ to leave the panel edges, and their radial-wall corners, to the
exchange and the refresh. A function you install yourself on a tangential face of a cubed-sphere block keeps that face
physical whatever its name, so it must write the corner itself. The predicate is
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}):

```cpp
    auto physical = [&](int face) {
      if (face < 0 || face >= static_cast<int>(fns.size()) || !fns[face])
        return false;
      // Cubed-sphere horizontal custom callbacks are built-in no-ops:
      // exchange owns these faces and their radial wall intersections.
      // Check callback identity, not its name, to retain genuine custom BCs.
      if (options->layout()->type() == "cubed-sphere" && face >= 2 &&
          is_custom_noop(fns[face]))
        return false;
      return !(static_cast<size_t>(face) < names.size() &&
               names[face].compare(0, 8, "periodic") == 0);
    };
```

and the identity test ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp is_custom_noop >}}):

```cpp
bool is_custom_noop(bcfunc_t const& func) {
  using Pointer =
      void (*)(torch::Tensor const&, int, snap::BoundaryFuncOptions);
  auto ptr = func.target<Pointer>();
  return ptr && (*ptr == custom_inner || *ptr == custom_outer);
}
```

The slab rule, after the one-call branch of a `reflecting` wall, is
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}):

```cpp
      for (int f = 0; f < nface; ++f) {
        if (!fns[f] || is_outflow(fns[f])) continue;
        ...
          if (any_orth && all_owned && static_cast<size_t>(f) < names.size() &&
              names[f].compare(0, 10, "reflecting") == 0) {
            fns[f](field, spatial, op);
            continue;
          }
        ...
        for (int orth = 1; orth <= 3; ++orth) {
          ...
          int g = ng < n / 2 ? ng : n / 2;
          int inner = (3 - orth) * 2;
          if (!physical(inner)) fns[f](field.narrow(orth, 0, g), spatial, op);
          if (!physical(inner + 1))
            fns[f](field.narrow(orth, n - g, g), spatial, op);
        }
      }
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | a resting polytrope uniform in $x_2$ with viscosity keeps $\max\lvert v_2\rvert/c_s$ and $\max\lvert\mathbf v\rvert/c_s$ small, for the stock wall and a user-named wall | $10^{-12}$ | rest to round-off |
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | a two-block $x_2$ split equals one block | exactly 0 | bitwise |
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | the scalar corner primitive matches its conserved value | exactly 0 | bitwise |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | `is_custom_noop` accepts the registered `custom_inner` and `custom_outer` and refuses `reflecting_inner`, an empty function and a caller's lambda | exact | Boolean result |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | cubed sphere, built-in `custom` on $x_2$/$x_3$: every $x_1$ ghost row inside the panel halos equals the reflecting mirror of the interior with `IVX` negated, at each depth; interiors unchanged | exactly 0 | bitwise (`torch::equal`); a copy and a sign change |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | cubed sphere, a caller's lambda on the four tangential faces: those rows keep the sentinel $-777$ in `IDN`, `IPR` and `IVX` (no refresh) | exactly 0 | bitwise (`torch::equal`) |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | the same deck as `layout: slab`, `type: cartesian`: those rows keep the sentinel (no reclassification off the cubed sphere) | exactly 0 | bitwise (`torch::equal`) |

: Tests of the corner refresh. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-tests}

The `test_wb_wall_corner` cases are `x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero` and `user_wall_keeps_u2_zero` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.user_wall_keeps_u2_zero >}}, {{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero >}}),
`x2_split_matches_one_block_exactly` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_split_matches_one_block_exactly >}}) and
`scalar_corner_primitive_matches_conserved` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.scalar_corner_primitive_matches_conserved >}}), each with a `_cuda` twin that
skips without a GPU. One process.

The `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` cases are `custom_noop_callback_identity`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.custom_noop_callback_identity >}}), which builds no mesh,
and three that share one helper, `check_radial_halo_refresh`:
`radial_walls_refresh_exchange_owned_horizontal_halos`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.radial_walls_refresh_exchange_owned_horizontal_halos >}}),
`radial_refresh_preserves_genuine_custom_horizontal_callbacks`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.radial_refresh_preserves_genuine_custom_horizontal_callbacks >}})
and `radial_refresh_does_not_reclassify_slab_custom_noops`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.radial_refresh_does_not_reclassify_slab_custom_noops >}}).
The deck is the card of `write_card` ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp write_card >}}): gnomonic-equiangle,
`reflecting` on both $x_1$ faces and `custom` on the four tangential faces, one block per panel, all six in one process,
edited to $n_{x_1} = 8$ and $n_g = 3$ with $n_{x_2} = n_{x_3} = 8$. Every $x_1$ ghost cell starts at the sentinel
$-777$, each block runs its own `exchange_ghost_zones` on a thread, and the assertions skip the $x_2$-$x_3$ diagonal
corners, which the face exchange also leaves out. The caller's-lambda case installs one empty lambda on faces 2 to 5 and leaves the
boundary names `custom`. The slab case keeps the same cards on one `slab` block with `type: cartesian`, so its
`custom` faces are outer edges that construction keeps. None of the four cases has a `_cuda` twin; they run on CPU
in one process.

None of these cases was run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence); the tolerances are the tests' own
assertions.

**Layout coverage.** `test_wb_wall_corner` declares `layout: slab` with `type: cartesian` in every case, so it
asserts the rule on the Cartesian layout. `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` asserts it on the cubed sphere, for the
built-in `custom` faces and for a caller's function on them, and checks on `slab` that step 2 of the Derivation does
not fire there. It is **untested on spherical-polar** as a corner assertion. The spherical-polar path is exercised
without being asserted by `test_x1_centroid_rest_python`, whose deck is reflecting on $x_1$ and $x_2$ and periodic on
$x_3$ with $n_{x_2}=n_{x_3}=4$: the two $x_3$ slabs are refreshed and the two $x_2$ slabs are skipped as physical, and
the test asserts that the column stays at rest, not what the corners hold. No cubed-sphere case uses an $x_1$
function other than `reflecting`, so the per-slab branch is not asserted on the cubed sphere.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` does not refresh corners; only the block's per-stage sync does.
- Only $x_1$ walls are refreshed; $x_2$-$x_3$ corners are synthesised (@sec-ch03-exchange).
- On the cubed sphere a panel seam is refreshed only where the tangential face holds the built-in `custom` no-op. A
  face named `reflecting` (the default when the card names none) or anything else, and a caller's own function under
  any name, count as physical: their radial-wall corners are left to that function and the exchange.
- The refresh's `physical` and `is_physical_boundary` disagree on a cubed-sphere panel edge that holds the built-in
  no-op: the refresh calls it exchange-owned, the predicate calls it physical (@sec-ch03-physfaces).
- On `slab` and `cubed` a `custom` face that construction keeps, an outer edge, counts as physical while writing
  nothing, so the refresh skips its $x_1$-wall corners: they keep what the $x_1$ function wrote in `apply_boundaries`
  from a ghost column that nothing writes (read from the code; the slab case above asserts the skip).
:::

The `Mesh`-level sync is a plain exchange ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} for `exchange_ghost_zones`). A user boundary
function that breaks the contract would write wrong corners without an error (read from the code; not measured). The
cubed-sphere refresh with an $x_1$ function other than `reflecting`, and on more than one block per panel, is not
tested. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
